added_models.model: Multi-species allometric scaling plus Simcyp PBPK prediction of pracinostat human oral PK, from mouse/rat/dog in-vivo PK and human in-vitro ADME (S*BIO, Jayaraman 2011)

dose.model: Multi-species allometric scaling plus Simcyp PBPK prediction of pracinostat human oral PK, from mouse/rat/dog in-vivo PK and human in-vitro ADME (S*BIO, Jayaraman 2011)
dose.population: Unselected (model: mouse, rat, dog PK; human microsomes, hepatocytes, Caco-2)
dose.quote: The oral bioavailability was 34, 65, and ∼3% in mice, dogs, and rats, respectively.
dose.note: Mouse, rat and dog PK plus human in-vitro ADME fed Simcyp and allometry to predict pracinostat's human oral PK; no efficacy exposure or tolerability margin stated.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Drug Metab Dispos, paywalled, not in PMC). 2011 is a publication proxy: the ADME work is IND-enabling by nature and the first-in-human studies started in 2007 (NCT00741234 2007-04, NCT00504296 2007-09), but the date the Simcyp/allometric prediction was run is not public. Pracinostat never reached an NDA, so model_filed is unknown.
dose.judgement: Split from pracinostat-mouse-xenograft under this run's identity rule: a genuinely different system (three-species in-vivo PK and human in-vitro ADME run through Simcyp and allometry, no tumour) making a different prediction (human CL, Vss, bioavailability and the oral PK profile, not tumour growth or tumour acetylation). Same precedent as famitinib-pbpk-rat-monkey-human-pk and gdc0980-genentech-translational-pkpd in this run. The draft's dose entry 2 (Jayaraman 2011, same) sits on the xenograft model_id and is the entry this track re-keys; removing it there is the adjudicator's edit.

engagement.note: SB939 acH3 tracked dose in HCT-116 and HL-60 mouse tissues; in 30 solid-tumour phase 1 patients PBMC acH3 rose with dose (10-80 mg).
engagement.quote: When applied to PBMCs from 30 patients with advanced solid malignancies in a phase I clinical trial, a dose-dependent (10-80 mg) increase in relative acH3 was observed 3-hour postdose on day 1
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Mol Cancer Ther, PMID 21586629, epub 2011-05-17, print 2011-07-01). Subjects are solid-tumour patients, not MDS; engagement admits any dosed humans. The same paper reports the mouse tissue data, so the comparison is stated.
engagement.judgement: Stated comparison: the authors measured the same acH3 Western readout in the xenograft/orthotopic HL-60 mice and in phase 1 PBMCs and conclude the PD 'translated from preclinical models to patients'; the readout moved with dose (r=0.97 with Cmax/AUC), so same. The later Abaza 2017 entry (adjudicated same) follows it on this track.
engagement.magnitude_basis: Relative acH3 in PBMCs vs SB939 dose and plasma Cmax/AUC

considered_not_added: Jayaraman 2011 identity (checker rule question 4): split into its own in_silico dose track (above) because the system (mouse/rat/dog PK plus human in-vitro ADME through Simcyp and allometry) and the prediction (human oral PK) are both different from the HCT-116/MOLM-13 xenograft efficacy-PD model; the draft's dose entry 2 on pracinostat-mouse-xenograft is the one this track replaces and is left for the adjudicator to remove or re-key. No derived 2017 contra is written on the new track: the effective-exposure claim that failed belongs to the xenograft track, which already carries it.

SB939 tissue-acH3 PD paper (Mol Cancer Ther 2011, 10.1158/1535-7163.mct-11-0044, epub 2011-05-17): HCT-116 xenograft and HL-60 orthotopic SCID mice, acH3 in tumour, PBMC, marrow; same system as pracinostat-mouse-xenograft, so no new track. It is, however, a comparison_stated engagement source the draft lacks: PBMC acH3 rose dose-dependently (10-80 mg) in 30 solid-tumour phase 1 patients, r=0.97 with Cmax/AUC, and the authors state the PK/PD 'are translated from preclinical models to patients'. A 2011 same (solid-tumour subjects) before the 2017 Abaza contra on that track is the adjudicator's edit.

HL-60 cells plus trial PBMCs (Int J Oncol 2014, 10.3892/ijo.2014.2555, epub 2014-07-22): azacitidine plus panobinostat induced NUR77/p21 in HL-60 and early NUR77/p21 induction in patient PBMCs from the Tan 2014 phase Ib/II correlated with response. Same system as panobinostat-leukemia-cells (human AML cell lines, HDACi plus HMA), so no new track; it would make the existing 2014 engagement entry a stated comparison (comparison_stated true) rather than a pairing.

ATF3 as marker of pracinostat response (Mol Cancer Ther 2016, 10.1158/1535-7163.mct-15-0890): solid-tumour cell lines, no MDS patient comparison (checker finding confirmed by the 34-title pracinostat sweep).
Ex vivo synergy screen in hematologic malignancies (SLAS Discov 2024, 10.1016/j.slasd.2023.12.001): no patient-outcome comparison for a member drug, run after the MDS results were known.
MDS/AML PDX azacitidine-venetoclax resistance (Front Oncol 2024, 10.3389/fonc.2024.1414950): panobinostat is not the dosed subject; no member patient comparison.

Ivaltinostat (CG200745/CG-745): 19 title hits are prostate, NSCLC, pancreatic and cholangiocarcinoma lines, rat/mouse cardiac, kidney and lung fibrosis models, the 2015 FIH in solid tumours, the 2022 pancreatic phase 1/2 and the 2024 CG-750 oral vs IV PK study; no AML or MDS model exists and NCT02737462 (phase 1/2 with azacitidine in MDS) has no results (status UNKNOWN). No track.

Panobinostat population PK (Savelieva 2015, 10.1007/s00228-015-1846-7): nonlinear mixed-effect model fitted to 7834 samples from 581 patients in 14 trials; a description of patient data with no preclinical prediction, so not a model system compared with patients.

Panobinostat PBPK DDI model (Drug Metab Dispos 2017, 10.1124/dmd.117.076851): built on clinical PK including the ketoconazole DDI study, then used to predict rifampin and midazolam interactions in lieu of trials for the Farydak label. In silico, but it predicts DDI magnitudes rather than a dose or exposure target, was built after the clinical data (a retrodiction at best), and serves myeloma labelling; no MDS patient comparison. Any regulator reliance it represents belongs to the myeloma context, not this one.

Beat AML / FIMM-style ex-vivo drug-sensitivity panels that include panobinostat: AML cohorts; no MDS patient was dosed with a member drug and compared with an ex-vivo readout (the targeted members x myelodysplastic x ex-vivo search returned only the three papers above).

George 2004 (Blood, epub 2004-10-28: K562, MV4-11, primary CML-BC and AML cells) and Giles 2006 (Clin Cancer Res, print 2006-08-01: H3/H2B acetylation in CD34+ blasts, 13 AML, 1 MDS, 1 ALL): first use and earliest patient comparison of the system already tracked as panobinostat-leukemia-cells; the re-dating to 2004/2006 is the checker's correction on the existing track, not a new system.
Panobinostat non-human-primate CSF/plasma PK (DIPG) and mouse blood-brain-barrier PK models: other indications, no MDS comparison.

Regulator documents: only the Farydak myeloma label (205353) is in the bundle; no MDS regulator document exists for any member, and no in-vitro or model data were relied on for MDS. No human challenge or human genetic model applies to this class.
